_comment: Mutations for the notification SSE stream: the broadcaster's fan-out and cap, and the route's framing and timing. The scenario harness is the only one that can see any of the route's behaviour — a stream has no response to compare — and the unit harness carries the broadcaster's queue and audience rules, which need two subscribers in one process and so cannot be reached over HTTP at all. The rate-limit ordering harness cannot be used: it issues limit+1 requests and reads each response, and a stream has no end to read to. That the route carries Python's 60/minute at all is checked statically by ratelimit_parity.py.

mutations.name: the keepalive waits half a minute
mutations._why: Both stacks wait 25s. A longer wait looks perfect until an intermediary with a 30s idle timeout starts dropping the connections.

mutations.name: the keepalive is an empty data frame
the greeting is skipped
mutations._why: Without it a client waits up to 25 seconds before anything proves the stream is live.

mutations.name: the greeting names the wrong field
the frames are not separated by a blank line
mutations._why: One newline is a continuation, not an event boundary; every frame would coalesce into one the client never dispatches.

mutations.name: the stream is served as plain text
nginx is allowed to buffer the stream
mutations._why: The header is the whole reason the stream arrives at all behind a proxy, and nothing about the response looks wrong without it.

mutations.name: the cap is off by one
the cap counts every org together
mutations._why: One busy org would then lock every other org out of its own bell.

mutations.name: the cap is the fallback rather than the plan's
a slot is not freed when a stream closes
an admin-only event reaches every subscriber
mutations._why: Node health, member changes and key audit events are admin-audience. This is the one mutation here that is a tenant-visible leak rather than a nuisance.

mutations.name: an admin-only event drops its viewers
mutations._why: Returning false rather than true unsubscribes every viewer the first time an admin event goes out.

mutations.name: an event crosses into another org
the fan-out waits for a full queue
mutations._why: blocking_send from inside the lock would deadlock the process; dropping is the behaviour, and it has to be the Full case specifically.

mutations.name: the queue is a tenth as deep
the broadcast goes out before the insert
mutations._why: A subscriber would then see a notification whose row can still fail, and whose id is zero.
mutations.equivalent: Nothing that reaches a stream calls create_notification yet — every emitter is still on the Python side of the proxy — so no harness can see the broadcast at all. Kept in the spec, unmarked, from the commit that wires the first emitter; until then it is a placeholder for a case that cannot exist.
